name: settings-tab-row-keyboard-focus-ring
description: Review (HIGH), targets the HTML rail: the settings rail's focus ring must be visible to a keyboard user who TABS onto a row, a WCAG 2.4.7 concern independent of the sibling scenario (which covers click-driven selection, not focus). settings.js renders the rail as plain <button data-pane> elements with no role/tabindex/outline overrides, so keyboard focus is native <button> :focus-visible - shown on Tab arrival, not on the click that opens the window. Enables Full Keyboard Access (AppleKeyboardUIMode=2 - Chromium on macOS, like Safari, only makes buttons Tab-stops when this is on) and opens Settings; nothing calls .focus() on open, so 'opened' trivially has no ring. Measured directly: this settings Widget has no other native View to hand focus to, so a lone Tab+Shift-Tab from a fresh open lands the ring on the LAST tabbable element in the page (the General pane's 'Warn before quitting' toggle), not back on the rail - Shift-Tab wraps within the single WebContentsView rather than landing where a naive reading of 'tab off, tab back' would expect. Rewritten to Tab twice (General -> Appearance) then Shift-Tab once (back to General), so the capture proves a real keyboard re-arrival ON THE ROW ITSELF, the case the HIGH fix actually targets.

actions.note: let the browser window finish first paint
Atrium MUST be frontmost or cmd+comma opens Finder Settings instead - observed
open Settings; its menu item is not reachable from a scenario
window opens on General - installSettings() never calls .focus(), so nothing is focused yet
ring must be OFF - document.activeElement is still body, not a keyboard arrival
with Full Keyboard Access on, this is the FIRST Tab in the page: it lands on the rail's first button, General (DOM order: the <nav> rail is appended before the <section> body)
second Tab moves forward onto the rail's second button, Appearance - deliberately leaving General so the next step is a real re-arrival rather than a no-op
moves focus back ONTO General - a real keyboard arrival, the exact case the HIGH fix targets
ring must be ON over General - focus returned to it via Tab/Shift-Tab, not a click or an arrow key

assertions.desc: region and origin re-measured against the actual HTML settings window (centered on screen, 860x620 - atrium_settings_window.cc), not the old SwiftUI assumption of a 900x600 window at (0,110). The old region [100,285,70,60] sampled pure white (mean 255,255,255, var 0.00): it was never over the window. This one is the General rail row alone (x=85-292, y=81-110), matching the sibling scenario's x-span but only one row tall, so a ring on Appearance instead (a wiring mistake) would not register here. min_delta re-measured with pixcmp on the actual before/after frames.
assertions.note: Re-measured 2026-08-16. The old region (x 85-292, y 81-110) no longer covers any rail button - it samples the empty page body beside the heading. This is the General button in the top bar, the first thing Tab still lands on.

assertions.desc: Cmd+Q still quits with the settings window open and Full Keyboard Access enabled - the atrium_surface_key_route fix, which this scenario covers
